hints.title: Centre the rectangle
hints.body: Sketch both curves. Imagine the rectangle’s vertical side furthest from the y-axis is a units away. Reflect that side across the y-axis to make a centred rectangle.
hints.recap: Reflection in the y-axis preserves a region whose boundary curves are even functions.
hints.pitfall: A symmetric drawing alone is not a proof of a maximum.
hints.pause: Explain why this centred rectangle can be at least as wide without losing height.

recall.reminder: Reflection in the y-axis preserves a region whose boundary curves are even functions.

hints.title: Write the area using a
hints.body: For the centred rectangle, find its full width and the vertical gap between the curves at x=a. Multiply them to form the area.
hints.recap: Translate a geometric condition into lengths or areas before deciding what it forces.
hints.pause: Write the area function and the values of a for which its height is positive.

recall.reminder: Translate a geometric condition into lengths or areas before deciding what it forces.

hints.title: Find and check the maximum
hints.body: Differentiate your area function. Find its positive stationary point and check that the area increases before it and decreases after it.
hints.recap: A positive-to-negative change of derivative gives a maximum.
hints.pitfall: The question asks for an area, not the value of a.
hints.pause: Substitute the valid stationary value into the area function.

recall.reminder: A positive-to-negative change of derivative gives a maximum.

solution:
A largest rectangle may be taken symmetric about the vertical axis. To justify this, let a be the larger absolute value of the two horizontal endpoint coordinates of any candidate. Its width is at most 2a, and its height is at most (8−2a2)−(a2−2)=10−3a2. The centred rectangle with endpoints −a,a attains both bounds.

Thus maximise A(a)=2a(10−3a2)=20a−6a3 for 0<a<10/3. Its derivative is A′(a)=20−18a2, so the positive stationary point is a=10/3.

The derivative is positive before this value and negative after it within the domain, so this is the maximum. Its area is 2103(10−103)=40109. Answer H.
